title: A patch or a silicone logo – which detail suits your garment?
seoTitle: Custom Clothing Patches and Silicone Branding
description: Compare sewn patches and raised silicone branding by edge finish, flexibility, placement and attachment on the final garment.
author: BEWE4R team
intro: A separate patch can give a logo a defined shape and border. A silicone detail can provide a raised, tactile mark, either as a separate badge or through another application method proposed by the producer. Ask to see how the specific detail attaches. “Silicone logo” tells you about the material or effect but leaves the construction open.

bodyHtml:
Choose the position before the badge

A firm badge can sit neatly on a structured jacket panel and feel uncomfortable on a stretch sleeve near the elbow. Hold a same-size paper shape on a worn sample. Mark the direction of stretch, the nearest seam and the point where the garment folds. If the detail sits over a pocket, open the pocket with the badge in position.

Send artwork that explains the edges

For a shield-shaped patch, distinguish the outline of the patch from any stitched border and from the logo inside it. Supply finished dimensions and indicate which colours or raised areas must stay separate. Ask how much usable space is left after the attachment or border is allowed for. Small lettering may need a different version at sleeve size than at chest size.

Option to examineWhat to ask the producer to show
Sewn badgeEdge finish, stitch line and reverse of the garment after attachment
Applied silicone detailProfile, flexibility and proposed attachment on the intended fabric
Badge near a seam or openingOne made-up garment showing pocket access, comfort and alignment

Handle the finished trial

Bend and move the sample as the wearer would. Check for a lifted corner, a hard edge or a stretch panel being held rigid. Put the sample through the agreed care routine and inspect again. If the base fabric or attachment method changes, review the combination again even if the artwork stays identical.

How do you describe the size of a patch with an irregular outline?

Provide the maximum finished width and height, a drawing at intended scale and an outline showing where stitching or attachment is allowed. Identify any corners that must remain free. A supplier quoting the width of the visible logo may interpret the size differently from someone measuring the outer border of the complete badge.

Make reorders unambiguous

Keep the badge reference and the garment placement drawing together. A reorder can match the badge perfectly and still place it on the wrong sleeve. Identify left and right from the wearer’s perspective and specify the finished placement landmark. View BEWE4R’s patch and silicone examples or send a drawing of the proposed placement.
